package_info.why_malicious: These packages are proof-of-concept (PoC) dependency confusion attacks that attempt to exfiltrate system information or download and execute code from external servers. While no outright malicious payload is present, the behavior is consistent with supply chain attack techniques and poses a risk to internal systems if installed.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code sends an HTTP GET request to a remote server using the package name as part of the URL, confirming installation and potentially leaking internal package usage.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code attempts to contact an external server during installation, which is not expected for internal dependencies and can be used to confirm internal usage or exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not make unsolicited network requests during installation, especially to non-standard domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may check for updates or telemetry, but this is rare for internal-only dependencies.
key_indicators: Network request to external domain at install time
Use of package name in remote URL (dependency confusion indicator)
No functional code, only network beacon

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects system information (CPU, home directory, hostname, username, DNS servers, package metadata) and sends it via HTTPS POST to an external server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates detailed system and environment information to an external domain without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not collect and transmit host information on import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry in some analytics packages, but always with user consent and clear documentation.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed via dependency confusion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of postinstall or import-time code

attack_chain.action: Code executes network beacon or exfiltrates system information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Confirmation of internal package usage or data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Attacker receives confirmation or system data, potentially enabling further targeted attacks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: internal reconnaissance or proof-of-concept demonstration

behavioral_signatures: Network requests to external domains during install or import
Collection and exfiltration of system environment data
Use of package name in remote URLs (dependency confusion indicator)
file_indicators: Presence of app.js or index.js with unsolicited network code
References to external domains in package source
References to os, dns, or process environment in package code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that make network requests during installation or import, especially to non-standard or suspicious domains. Flag packages that collect and transmit system or environment information. Use static analysis to detect references to os, dns, and network modules in package entry points. Block packages with postinstall scripts or code that contacts external servers using the package name.
